- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later days.
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in the history (e.g., after 69.51 or 70.80), leading to inflated forecasts that fail to capture subsequent mean reversion.
- Underestimates the true mean trend in the final 10–15 days of the forecast, particularly when the true outcome shows strong upward momentum.
- Tends to lag behind the true trend by 1–3 days, especially in the middle of the forecast window.
- Overreacts to recent high values in history, producing overly optimistic forecasts that don’t reflect the true volatility or mean reversion.
- Underestimates the magnitude of upward momentum in the final 5–10 days, especially when the true outcome shows accelerating growth.
- Forecasts are too smooth; fail to capture sudden reversals or sharp corrections in the true outcome.
- Model exhibits a “peak bias” around day 10–15 of the forecast, where it overestimates the peak and then underestimates the decline or plateau.
